Question Choices: A rectangle is 3/5 m tall and 4/7 m wide. Find the area. Give your answer as a fraction only, no units.
Hints: Multiply height by width. Metres times metres gives square metres.
Solution: 3/5 x 4/7 = (3/5) x (4/7) = 12/35. Simplified result: 12/35. Answer: 12/35 square metres.

Question Choices: Select. When a rectangle's height and width are measured in meters (m), what unit should the area be measured in? ~~meters | square-meters~~
Hints: Multiply height by width. Metres times metres gives square metres.
Solution: Height in metres times width in metres gives square metres: m x m=m².

Question Choices: If a rectangle is split into 4 equal rows and 7 equal columns, how many equal small rectangles are there in total?
Hints: Multiply equal rows by columns to count all cells.
Solution: 4 equal rows x 7 equal columns=28 small rectangles.

Question Choices: A rectangle is 3 m tall and 4 m wide. It is split into 5 equal rows (tall) and 8 equal columns (wide). What are the height and width of each small rectangle? Give your answers as fractions only, no units.
Hints: Divide whole dimensions to find one cell; multiply cell dimensions to recover the whole.
Solution: Height = 3 / 5 = 3/5 m. Width = 4 / 8 = 1/2 m. Keep rows with height and columns with width.

Question Choices: A 1 m x 1 m large square is divided into several equal rectangles. If each small rectangle is 1/24 of the whole square, what is the area of one small rectangle in square meters? Give your answer as a fraction only, no units.
Hints: Find the whole area, then divide it equally among the stated number of parts.
Solution: The whole square has area 1 m x 1 m=1 square metre. Divide into 24 equal parts:1/24 square metre per part.
